extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, participating employers, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), Office of Apprenticeship (OA), small business representatives, and commenters on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory analysis and Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) accompanying a proposed rule revising 29 CFR part 29 for registered apprenticeship and registered CTE apprenticeship, including cost estimates, alternatives considered, and impacts on small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-point assessments requirement (proposed § 29.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: End-point assessments are required under the proposed rule as a key method for sponsors to assess the skills and knowledge acquired by the apprentice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department rationale: End-point assessments "help to measure and ensure the quality of registered apprenticeship programs." Costing: baseline includes end-point assessment costs; alternative removing them reduces annualized costs to $41.8 million (7% discount) and total $293.8 million (7% discount) over 10 years. Department decision: not to remove because assessments are key to quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program reviews frequency and scope (proposed § 29.19 — every 5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule requires program reviews for all registered apprenticeship programs on a 5-year cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Ensures high-quality programs, that programs abide by regulatory requirements, and balances Department resources and burden on programs. Costing: baseline included program reviews every 5 years; Department concluded all programs should be reviewed over a 5-year period rather than for-cause only or more frequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative 1 — Remove end-point assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory alternative that would remove the requirement for end-point assessments from the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost impact: Estimated reduction in costs — annualized $41.8 million at 7% discount; total $293.8 million (7%). Department decision: not pursued because end-point assessments are key to assessing apprentice skills and ensuring program quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative 2 — Conduct program reviews only for cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory alternative to conduct program reviews only for cause (rather than for all sponsors every 5 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumptions used: instead of all sponsors reviewed every 5 years, only 320 sponsors would receive program reviews each year; assumed 20% of those reviews find noncompliance requiring a compliance action plan. Cost impact: annualized costs $127.9 million at 7%; total $898.2 million at 7% over 10 years. Department decision: not pursued because for-cause-only reviews would miss many programs that may need reviews and would not ensure high-quality compliance across all programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative 3 — Program reviews every 2 years
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory alternative to increase review frequency to all registered apprenticeship programs every 2 years instead of every 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational assumptions: increases annual program reviews by SAAs (from 3,085 to 7,713 in year 1) and OA (from 2,213 to 5,533). Cost impact: annualized costs $196.9 million at 7%; total $1,383.1 million at 7% over 10 years. Department decision: not pursued because increased frequency raises costs more than expected benefits and OA/SAAs would lack resources to conduct the needed reviews. Department requests comments on how OA could use resources more effectively to identify programs needing more frequent review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative 4 — Independent third-party end-point assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory alternative to require end-point assessments to be conducted by an independent third party rather than by sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: independent third-party assessments would remove perceived conflicts of interest and could increase program quality. Costing assumption: increased Training and Development Manager (private sector) time from 1 hour to 4 hours to reflect additional prep/synthesis/reporting by third party. Cost impact: annualized costs $646.3 million at 7%; total $4,539.5 million at 7% over 10 years. Department decision: not pursued because the burden on programs would be too high relative to benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status quo alternative (no regulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative of maintaining current rules (no changes to program standards, apprenticeship agreements, state governance requirements, and no registered CTE apprenticeship model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.O. 12866 requires agencies to assess the alternative of not regulating. Under status quo, there would be no new costs or benefits. Department decision: rejected because proposed rule is believed to improve capacity of the National Apprenticeship System, provide equitable pathways, and increase long-term resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: E.O. 12866 cost-benefit assessment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must assess all costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives, including the alternative of not regulating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to frame the analysis of alternatives and to quantify costs and benefits across regulatory options (including status quo). The Department's E.O. 12866 analysis quantifies labor costs and other impacts and informs the IRFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFA / IRFA requirement for significant economic impact on small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Flexibility Act requires an Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) when a proposed regulation will have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; the Department published an IRFA because it believes the proposed rule would have such impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Participation in registered apprenticeship is voluntary; only small entities that choose to participate would experience impacts. The Department still analyzes impacts because it expects a substantial number of small entities could be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance requirements imposed on registered apprenticeship program sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated types of labor and administrative costs the proposed rule would impose on program sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed items quantified in the E.O. 12866 analysis: (1) rule familiarization; (2) on-the-job training documentation; (3) wage analysis and career development; (4) data collection and reporting; (5) program registration; (6) program standards and adoption agreement; (7) end-point assessments; (8) program reviews. Also recorded: additional recordkeeping costs imposed on participating employers. First-year per-sponsor estimates cited (examples): rule familiarization $412; OJT documentation $1,031 (for programs <2,000 OJT hours); wage analysis $206 (per new/revised occupation determination); data collection/reporting $111; program registration $103 (new program); program standards adoption agreement $103 (new non-CBA standards); end-point assessments $103 per sponsor per apprentice; program reviews $842 per noncompliant sponsor; recordkeeping $138 per employer. Department seeks comment on these estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance requirements imposed on registered CTE apprenticeship program sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated labor and administrative costs quantified for registered CTE apprenticeship sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items: (1) rule familiarization; (2) program registration application requirements; (3) selection of a diverse and inclusive cross-section of students; (4) sponsor oversight; (5) apprenticeship agreements; (6) program reviews; (7) request for reconsideration of program registration status; (8) data and quality metrics. First-year per-sponsor estimates cited (examples): rule familiarization $412; registration application requirements $1,031; selection of diverse students $74; sponsor oversight $913; apprenticeship agreements $17 per sponsor per apprentice; program reviews $842 per noncompliant sponsor; request for reconsideration $619; data and quality metrics $495. Department seeks comment on these estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost estimation methodology (analysis period, discounting, and dollars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological choices used to estimate costs and annualize totals over the analysis period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis period: 10 years. Discount rates: annualized outputs reported at 3% and 7% discount rates. Dollar year: 2022 dollars. Outputs presented as year-by-year costs, annualized costs, and total (10-year) costs under each alternative and the NPRM baseline (exhibits provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection of number of sponsors and participating employers (use in cost estimation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual projected counts of registered apprenticeship program sponsors and participating employers and registered CTE apprenticeship sponsors and participating employers over the 10-year analysis period (Exhibit 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from exhibit: Year 1 — 26,492 registered apprenticeship program sponsors and 40,533 participating employers; Year 10 — 34,970 sponsors and 53,504 participating employers; CTE sponsors grow from 137 (Year 1) to 3,841 (Year 10). These projections underlie aggregate cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for quantifying impact on small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to determine whether the proposed rule would have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities in each industry and size class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps used: (1) use SBA Table of Small Business Size Standards to set size thresholds; (2) obtain number of firms, employees, and annual revenue by industry and firm size from Census Bureau's Statistics of U.S. Businesses; (3) convert revenue data from 2017 to 2022 dollars using the GDP deflator; (4) divide estimated first-year and annualized cost per sponsor by average annual receipts per firm to determine percent-of-receipts impact; (5) determine whether impact meets the 'significant economic impact' threshold and whether the affected firms constitute a substantial number of small firms by dividing number of firms in size category by total small firms in industry. The Department produced 19 industry tables applying this method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant economic impact threshold (3% of receipts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department treats a regulatory impact as 'significant' when the estimated cost per firm is 3 percent or more of average annual receipts for that firm size/industry category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied in the analysis: the Department reports which industries and size classes would experience first-year and annualized costs ≥3% of receipts and whether those firms constitute a substantial number of small entities (e.g., Agriculture: firms with receipts below $100,000 would see 5.7% first-year costs and constitute 18% of small firms in the industry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions used in program review and compliance-cost calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational and behavioral assumptions used to estimate numbers of reviews, noncompliance rates, staff time, and similar inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: assumed 20% of program reviews find noncompliance and require a compliance action plan; Alternative 2 assumes 320 sponsors receive reviews per year; Alternative 3 assumes SAAs conduct 7,713 reviews (up from 3,085) and OA 5,533 (up from 2,213) in year 1; Alternative 4 increases Training and Development Manager time from 1 hour to 4 hours to account for third-party assessment preparation and reporting. These assumptions are explicitly stated and used to adjust cost calculations across alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated per-sponsor and per-firm cost metrics and participating employer thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative monetary estimates used to evaluate per-firm burden and thresholds for significant impact on participating employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Estimated first-year cost per registered apprenticeship program sponsor (7% discount) = $3,420; annualized cost per sponsor (7% discount) = $3,238. For registered CTE sponsors: first-year $3,476; annualized $2,398. Estimated costs borne by participating employers (rule familiarization + recordkeeping) = $343.69 per participating employer in registered apprenticeship; participating employer revenue would need to be less than $11,400 for the participating employer to experience a 'significant economic impact' from those costs; for registered CTE participating employers the corresponding revenue threshold is $6,800.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and disclosure of unquantified costs and transfer payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgement of costs and effects that could not be quantified due to data limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of unquantified items: new requirements for off-the-job training; prohibition of non-disclosure and non-compete provisions; transfer payments from participating employers to apprentices in the form of compensation. The Department notes the existence of these possible impacts and invites comment where appropriate.
